sources.what: Matthew Arnold, Culture and Anarchy (1869): Preface and ch. IV 'Hebraism and Hellenism'
sources.note: The Hebraism and Hellenism argument is set out in ch. IV, not mainly the Preface: read ch. IV (with the Preface as context).

sources.what: Spengler, The Decline of the West (1918; English Atkinson 1926)
sources.note: Atkinson died 1960, after 1955: fails the rule even though Gutenberg (#72344) has it (US public domain). Our own words only.

sources.what: Solzhenitsyn, 'A World Split Apart', Harvard commencement address, 8 June 1978 (one short quotation); Edward Said, Orientalism (1978); Bernard Lewis, 'The Question of Orientalism' (New York Review of Books, 24 June 1982); Ibn Warraq, Defending the West (2007); Christopher Dawson, Religion and the Rise of Western Culture (1950); Larry Siedentop, Inventing the Individual (2014); Rémi Brague, Eccentric Culture (French 1992; English 2002); Roger Scruton, England and the Need for Nations (2004) and Our Church (2012) on 'oikophobia'; Tom Holland, Dominion (2019); Douglas Murray, The War on the West (2022); Vishal Mangalwadi, The Book That Made Your World (2011); Arnold Toynbee, A Study of History (1934-61)
sources.note: In copyright: our own words, at most one short quotation (under 25 words). Living voices (Siedentop, Brague, Holland, Murray, Mangalwadi): cite as listed and keep fair and non-partisan.

art.title: Church of Santa Maria della Febbre, Rome
art.why: A round, domed Roman building used as a church, with the obelisk before it: Rome's stones carrying Christian worship (the classical-Christian building the spec wants). The Pantheon interior is claimed by Come and see.

art.title: The Ponte Salario
art.why: A crumbling Roman bridge with plants in its stones and people living around it: the ruin of decline narratives, still in use.

art.title: Aleksandr Solzhenitsyn with Mstislav Rostropovich
art.why: REUSE of the existing Practice portrait, as the spec asks.

art.title: Rouen Cathedral, West Façade
art.why: A Gothic cathedral front soaring the height of the canvas in blue, peach and lavender. The NGA text does not say dawn: describe only its light and colours. Different version from the existing monet-rouen (Sunlight).
